dangerous_cpts.main_problem: The CVP entry for HIGH CVP given LOW LVEDVOLUME is the only parameter directly localized on a suspicious path and appears exclusively in failure scenarios. This makes the CVP CPT the strongest candidate for refinement with relatively limited risk of disrupting successful behavior.

suspicious_parameters.justification: Although HIGH CVP is physiologically rare when LVEDVOLUME is LOW, this parameter is activated only in failures and never in successes. A small upward adjustment is the least disruptive way to test whether the model is underestimating this exceptional but failure-relevant outcome.

dangerous_cpts.main_problem: LVEDVOLUME lies upstream of the suspicious CVP path and one activated entry is repeatedly present in failures, but it also appears frequently in successful cases and was not itself localized as suspicious by the path-wise analysis. It is therefore only a weak secondary candidate for search-space inclusion.

suspicious_parameters.justification: This entry corresponds to LOW LVEDVOLUME under No_Hypovolemia and no LVFAILURE, which may be somewhat overused if downstream CVP failures are being induced too often through this parent configuration. Because the parameter also supports many successes, only a slight decrease is justified and confidence remains weak.

cpt_danger_report.overall_summary: The best-supported refinement target is the CVP CPT, specifically HIGH CVP given LOW LVEDVOLUME. Evidence for a second CPT is limited, but LVEDVOLUME can be included as a low-priority secondary candidate because it is structurally upstream of the suspicious CVP behavior and the search space should contain at least two CPTs when some support exists.

dangerous_cpts.main_problem: The CVP CPT shows the strongest localized evidence of miscalibration on a suspicious path. Its reported entries conflict with the expected directional relation between LVEDVOLUME and CVP and are disproportionately associated with failures.

suspicious_parameters.justification: When LVEDVOLUME=LOW, HIGH CVP is physiologically discordant and this entry is much more failure-associated than success-associated. Lowering this probability is well supported and should reduce erroneous support for inconsistent CVP outcomes.
When LVEDVOLUME=HIGH, LOW CVP is directionally inconsistent and appears only in failures. Even though the count is smaller, the zero-success pattern makes this a credible refinement target.

dangerous_cpts.main_problem: The BP CPT is implicated at the endpoint of a suspicious hemodynamic path, especially for the target-inconsistent HIGH BP outcome under low cardiac output. The evidence is weaker than for CVP because the parameter is also often activated in successful cases and its local semantics are not obviously wrong.

suspicious_parameters.justification: For CO=LOW and TPR=NORMAL, HIGH BP is currently nearly excluded, yet repeated failures on this endpoint suggest the mapping may be too rigid for some cases. Only a slight increase is warranted because the entry is still commonly activated in successes and strong changes could disrupt otherwise coherent hemodynamics.

cpt_danger_report.overall_summary: CVP is the best-supported refinement target and should clearly be included in the search space. BP is the next most defensible CPT to include to satisfy the minimum of two supported CPTs, while upstream priors and intermediate volume/stroke-volume mappings remain too weakly isolated from successful behavior.

dangerous_cpts.main_problem: The suspicious evidence is concentrated on the HYPOVOLEMIA→LVEDVOLUME→CVP path, where CVP entries are activated only in failures and are physiologically discordant with the corresponding LVEDVOLUME states. This makes CVP the clearest refinement target with relatively low risk of disrupting successful behavior.

suspicious_parameters.justification: When LVEDVOLUME=LOW, HIGH CVP is strongly inconsistent with the expected filling-pressure relationship. Its activation is exclusive to failures, so reducing this already small probability is well supported.
When LVEDVOLUME=HIGH, LOW CVP is physiologically mismatched and appears only in failures. Further suppressing this rare but harmful assignment is a targeted refinement.

dangerous_cpts.main_problem: LVEDVOLUME contains a semantically questionable column under hypovolemia, but the same entries are also heavily activated in successes, so the evidence is mixed. It is still a reasonable secondary search-space candidate because it sits immediately upstream of the suspicious CVP behavior and may be contributing to mispropagation.

suspicious_parameters.justification: This column corresponds to HYPOVOLEMIA=Hypovolemia and LVFAILURE=FALSE, where assigning HIGH LVEDVOLUME with probability 0.9 is directionally counter to expected reduced filling. The strong success overlap argues for cautious rather than aggressive refinement.

This entry is less clearly faulty because LOW LVEDVOLUME under No_Hypovolemia and no LV failure can still occur, and it is common in successes. If included, only a mild decrease is justified to avoid harming currently successful inferences.

cpt_danger_report.overall_summary: CVP is the only strongly supported refinement target because its suspicious parameters are exclusive to failures and physiologically inconsistent. LVEDVOLUME is a weaker but still defensible secondary candidate due to its upstream role and one semantically problematic column, allowing the search space to cover at least two plausibly relevant CPTs.
